output.body: Take the practice problem sum(n) = 1 plus 2 plus up to n, where the base case is sum(1) = 1, the smallest input you can answer without calling the function. The recursive step is sum(n) = n plus sum(n minus 1), since adding n to the sum up to n minus 1 is the same problem one size smaller. Tracing sum(3) gives 3 plus sum(2), then 3 plus (2 plus sum(1)), then 3 plus (2 plus 1), which equals 6, so each call waits on a smaller one until the base case stops the chain.
output.key_idea: A recursive function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller input until it reaches a base case it can answer directly.
